findings.claim: The R2 repair's `(?!--from=)` exclusion is a strict coverage REGRESSION: a final-stage `COPY --from=build-identity /ctx/.git /app/.git` was RED under the round-1 substring scan and is GREEN now, shipping the git history into the public image — and the comment justifying the exclusion ("`--from=` sources copy from a stage, not from the context") is false for this Dockerfile, whose only named stage holds the entire context at `/ctx`.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py:6139-6141 `re.finditer(r"(?m)^COPY\s+(?!--from=)([^\n]*)$", final_text)` vs the round-1 line it replaced, `re.search(r"(?m)^COPY\s+[^\n]*\.git", final_text)`. Input: Dockerfile with `COPY --from=build-identity /ctx/.git /app/.git` inserted before `USER pwuser`. `build-identity` did `COPY . /ctx`, so `/ctx/.git` in that stage IS the context's git dir. The `copy_from` conjunct only requires one line ending `/app/BUILD_SHA`, so extra `--from=` lines are ungraded.
findings.repro: Orchestrator-verified: mutated Dockerfile -> `_check_build_sha_is_derived(dockerfile=...)` passed=True, while the round-1 regex would have flagged it (`round1_would_flag=True`).
findings.acceptance: A final-stage COPY naming `.git` is RED whether or not it carries `--from=` (the `.git` substring test applies to all COPY lines; only the whole-context `.` rule is `--from=`-exempt), demonstrated red-first with the `COPY --from=build-identity /ctx/.git /app/.git` mutation added as a self-test row; or the regression is named verbatim in the case's declared ceilings.

findings.claim: The new `final_stage_copies_git` conjunct is defeated by one character: `COPY ./ /app/`, `ADD . /app/` and `COPY --chown=pwuser . /app/` all ship the whole context (now including `.git`, since this PR removed it from `.dockerignore`) into the published image while every conjunct stays green, and none of these spellings is listed in the case's declared ceilings.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py:6139-6141 — the membership test is `(m.group(1).split() or [""])[0] == "."` plus a `.git` substring scan, over `^COPY\s+…` only. Inputs replacing the final-stage `COPY src/ /app/src/`: `COPY ./ /app/` (first token `./` != `.`), `ADD . /app/` (instruction not matched at all), `COPY --chown=pwuser . /app/` and `COPY --link . /app/` (first token is the flag). The self-test row only ever tries the literal `COPY . /app/`, so it proves the guard fires for one spelling, not for the property.
findings.acceptance: The final-stage rule normalises the source token (strip trailing `/`, skip leading `--flag=` options) and covers `ADD` as well as `COPY`, watched red with `COPY ./ /app/` and `ADD . /app/` as additional self-test rows; or those spellings are added verbatim to the triage note's declared ceilings.

findings.claim: The two new source-reading conjuncts disagree about what counts as "the whole context": `./` and option flags falsely REDDEN the derive-stage conjunct on a Dockerfile that builds and derives correctly, while the same spellings silently pass the final-stage conjunct (R7).
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py:6123-6128 — `src != "." and ".git" not in src`. Input: `COPY . /ctx` -> `COPY ./ /ctx` (identical Docker semantics) or `COPY --link . /ctx`; both report `derive_stage_never_copies_the_context`. Also, if the derive stage has two COPY lines into `/ctx` only the first is read, so a correct stage reddens.
findings.acceptance: Both conjuncts share one source-token normaliser, so `COPY ./ /ctx` is green and `COPY ./ /app/` is red; or the false-red spellings are named in the triage ceilings alongside the line-continuation one. NOTE: a shared normaliser written for R7 closes this incidentally — if so, record it fixed rather than as debt.
